clippings.speaker: Brian De Palma
clippings.quote: Pino Donaggio wrote the score for DON'T LOOK NOW. I was put on to him by a good friend of mine, the "Time" magazine film critic Jay Cocks, who had always liked his music and suggested him to me when Bernard Herrmann unfortunately passed away and I was looking for another composer. I listened to his records and talked it over with him and felt he was the right kind of combination.
clippings.title: Brian DePalma Cinefantastique interview
clippings.context: De Palma, interviewed by Mike Childs and Alan Jones for Cinefantastique (Vol. 6 No. 1, Summer 1977), explains how he found Donaggio for Carrie; transcribed on a fan site.

clippings.speaker: Brian De Palma
clippings.quote: Nobody writes those psycho dream things like Pino does, and there's a long section of Noomi's nightmare that has big surprises in it, and he's just the master of that. I mean, we did it in "Carrie," we did it in "Dressed to Kill," we did it in "Raising Cain."
clippings.title: Brian De Palma Q & A: 'Passion,' McAdams vs. Rapace, Sex Tools UPDATED (New Trailer)
clippings.context: Anne Thompson asks De Palma about reuniting with Donaggio on Passion, their first film together since Raising Cain.

clippings.speaker: Brian De Palma
clippings.quote: Well, I've worked with Pino on seven films together. He knows how to do these long violent sequences that I create. The last cue at the end of the film, when the last nightmare takes place, no one writes music like that but him.
clippings.title: Interview: Brian De Palma Talks Passion
clippings.context: Phone interview ahead of Passion's US release, asked about scoring the film with Donaggio.

clippings.speaker: Pino Donaggio
clippings.quote: When I first told De Palma that I was going to score Joe Dante's film he said: ''if you feel like it, ashkksss''. Well, he made an unfriendly noise. … But Brian De Palma didn't like it even one bit.
clippings.title: Interview with Pino Donaggio: Oorlogswinter (Winter in Wartime)
clippings.context: Donaggio, interviewed in Amsterdam about Oorlogswinter, recalls De Palma's reaction to him scoring Joe Dante's Piranha.

clippings.speaker: Pino Donaggio
clippings.quote: And of course I would have liked to do all other films by Brian de Palma. He keeps on changing composers, but there is still something out there. He came to Venice to talk to me about The Toyer.
clippings.title: Interview with Pino Donaggio: Oorlogswinter (Winter in Wartime)
clippings.context: Donaggio on the gaps in their collaboration and De Palma's unmade project The Toyer.

clippings.speaker: Pino Donaggio
clippings.quote: For a long time Brian didn't listen to anything before the recording: he heard the music directly in the studio, with the orchestra. There were no demos, there was nothing. He trusted me. The first time I was risking a lot, because he didn't know what I would do. In fact, the night before recording in New York, I didn't sleep much!
clippings.original: Per molto tempo Brian non ascoltava nulla prima della registrazione: sentiva la musica direttamente in sala, con l’orchestra. Non c’erano provini, non c’era niente. Si fidava. «La prima volta rischiavo molto, perché non sapeva che cosa avrei fatto. Infatti, la notte prima di registrare a New York, non è che abbia dormito molto!
clippings.title: Pino Donaggio: «Volevano far cambiare il finale di Blow Out». L'intervista esclusiva, da De Palma a Refn
clippings.context: Donaggio, interviewed by Alessandro Gamma, describes De Palma hearing his scores for the first time at the recording session; translated from Italian.

clippings.speaker: Pino Donaggio
clippings.quote: When we watched it with the American distributors, they wanted to have the ending changed. But Brian was very tough, he refused to change it.
clippings.original: Quando lo vedemmo con i distributori americani, volevano far cambiare il finale. Ma Brian fu durissimo, non volle cambiarlo.
clippings.title: Pino Donaggio: «Volevano far cambiare il finale di Blow Out». L'intervista esclusiva, da De Palma a Refn
clippings.context: Donaggio recalls the fight over Blow Out's bleak ending; translated from Italian.

clippings.speaker: Pino Donaggio
clippings.quote: Brian De Palma and I often joked around. He used to tell me: "I pulled you out of the canals of Venice".
clippings.original: Con Brian De Palma scherzavamo spesso. Lui mi diceva: “Ti ho tirato fuori dai canali di Venezia”.
clippings.title: Pino Donaggio: «Volevano far cambiare il finale di Blow Out». L'intervista esclusiva, da De Palma a Refn
clippings.context: Donaggio on a running joke between them; translated from Italian.
